title: fix(cluster): a Redis outage must not crash replicas; resync caches on reconnect
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-steve"} -->
_Requested by **Steve** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01FdL1XeUyvVNxLreh3F4Qi9?thread=cmsg_01FdL1XeUyvVNxLreh3F4Qi9AS1kFKtVB2ZTW2g1kt4zuU)_

Fixes #31596

Clause-②: yes (widening)
Metadata-protocol: none

Measured on the built declarations (`dist/index.d.ts` of each touched package): new exports in `@objectstack/service-cluster` (`CLUSTER_RESYNC_EVENT`, `ClusterDriverLiveness`, `offerClusterDriverLiveness`, `onClusterResync`, `readClusterDriverHealth`, `describeConnectionError`, `redactCredentials` and five types) and `@objectstack/service-cluster-redis` (`REDIS_COMMAND_TIMEOUT_MS`, `watchRedisConnection`, `describeRedisTarget`), optional members `RedisDriverOptions.logger`, `RedisPubSubOptions.liveness`, `DatasourceAdminServiceConfig.listConvergeNames` and the connector-credential door's `resyncFromCluster`, and public methods `MetadataManager.resyncClusterPubSub()`, `DatasourceAdminService.resyncDatasourceMutationPubSub()`, `AutomationEngine.resyncConnectorCredentialPubSub()`. Nothing is removed or made required. The claim read `no`; the measurement says `yes (widening)`. No metadata an author writes changes.

## 维护者速读

- 改了什么：多副本 Redis 集群下，Redis 宕机不再让副本进程崩溃；宕机只记一条告警，恢复后各缓存自动重新同步。
- 为什么改：此前定时任务拿不到集群锁时抛出未处理的拒绝，每个副本在下一次定时触发时退出；宕机期间丢失的缓存失效通知也要等到重启才会恢复。
- 风险与回滚：单节点（默认内存驱动）完全不变；Redis 驱动新增默认 2 秒命令超时，单条命令超过 2 秒会失败（驱动和共享缓存的命令都是 O(1)）。回滚即撤销本 PR。
- 先看：`service-job` 的 `cron-job-adapter.ts`（不再崩溃）和 `service-cluster` 的新文件 `cluster-resync.ts`（`cluster.resync` 事件）。
- 两分钟验证：在装有 redis-server 的机器上跑 `service-cluster-redis` 的 `redis-outage.real-redis.test.ts`，它会在两个运行中的内核下停掉再启动 Redis。
- 需要你做的：无；标题里的 `!` 是否保留由席位复核（见 Acceptance notes）。

## What changes

- **No crash on a dead lock (`@objectstack/service-job`).** `CronJobAdapter` leader-elects every scheduled fire on the cluster lock. A rejected `acquire` used to escape the timer callback as an unhandled rejection and end the process. It now skips that fire, and the next tick retries. A failed `release` is absorbed, and the lease expires on its TTL. The adapter logs one warning per lock outage and one info line when the lock answers again. No process-wide `unhandledRejection` handler is added. `runScheduled` is the only lock caller in the job adapters.
- **The driver watches its connections (`@objectstack/service-cluster-redis`).** The command connection and the pub/sub subscriber both get an `error` / `close` / `ready` listener (`watchRedisConnection`). ioredis no longer prints `Unhandled error event` per reconnect attempt. The driver logs one warning per outage, naming `host:port` and never the URL or a password, and one info line when the connection returns. New option `driverOptions.logger`.
- **Bounded commands.** `createRedisClient()` sets `commandTimeout: REDIS_COMMAND_TIMEOUT_MS` (2000 ms). ioredis arms it before offline queueing, so it bounds queued commands too. `client.duplicate()` inherits it, so the shared cache's derived connection is bounded as well.
- **Driver health and `cluster.resync` (`@objectstack/service-cluster`).** `ClusterDriverLiveness` is the connection state machine a remote driver feeds. Read health with `readClusterDriverHealth(cluster)`, which returns `{ driver, nodeId, state: 'unknown' | 'up' | 'down', since, outages, lastError? }`, or `undefined` on the memory driver. This is the accessor #31601 reads. When every failed connection is ready again, the liveness emits ONE local event, `cluster.resync` (`CLUSTER_RESYNC_EVENT`). Subscribe with `onClusterResync(cluster, handler)`, which returns a disposer. The event is never published to peers. On the memory driver the subscription is an inert no-op. #31597 joins here. The liveness is offered on the cluster instance under a `Symbol.for` key, as `driver-connection.ts` already does.
- **The four caches re-read on it.**
  - `MetadataClusterBridgePlugin` subscribes once and calls each attached lane's resync seam, with per-lane failure isolation:
    - metadata list caches: `MetadataManager.resyncClusterPubSub()` drops every list cache and the endpoint index; registry entries are kept.
    - datasource pools: `DatasourceAdminService.resyncDatasourceMutationPubSub()` re-converges every datasource in the shared rows plus every pool this replica holds.
    - connector credentials: `AutomationEngine.resyncConnectorCredentialPubSub()` runs the reconcile a peer's signal runs.
  - `AuthzClusterBridgePlugin` advances the engine's write epoch with reason `remote`, which retires cached grants exactly as a delivered remote hint does.

R3: the single-node default path is unchanged (the memory driver offers no liveness, so no listener, latch or resync runs on it). Nothing switches on by itself: every new path needs the redis driver connected, and the bridges still attach only when `isInProcessClusterDriver` is false. The split-brain guard is untouched, and the deploy README's "multi-node unsupported" line is untouched.

## Tests

- `service-cluster-redis/src/redis-outage.real-redis.test.ts` (new) uses a real `redis-server` with a password. It is skipped where the binary is absent. Two `LiteKernel` replicas, each with the redis cluster driver and a cron job on a 100 ms interval, share one Redis. The Redis process is SIGKILLed and restarted on the same port. Pinned:
  - no unhandled rejection;
  - exactly one "lost its connection" line and one "reconnected" line per replica, with no password anywhere;
  - at most one cron warning per replica;
  - no fire during the outage, and the next fire after the return runs;
  - a hint published during the outage is lost, and the peer converges on its single `cluster.resync`;
  - a hint published after the return reaches the peer.

  The second case dials a black-holed TCP server: a GET on the cache's `duplicate()`d connection rejects with `timed out` in about 2 s, not about 30 s.
- `service-cluster/src/cluster-resync.test.ts` (new) covers:
  - one warning per outage;
  - resync once, only when every failed source is back;
  - no resync on first connect;
  - handler isolation, `close()` and redaction;
  - the offer is non-enumerable;
  - CONTROL: the memory driver gives no health and an inert subscription.
- Each lane got a new describe:
  - `metadata-cluster-bridge-plugin.test.ts`: each lane is called once per outage, a failing lane is isolated, nothing runs after shutdown, and CONTROL memory.
  - `authz-cluster-bridge-plugin.test.ts`: one `bump('remote')` while bridged, nothing after shutdown, and CONTROL TTL 0.
  - `metadata-manager-cluster.test.ts`, `datasource-cluster-convergence.test.ts`, `connector-credential-cluster.test.ts`: a lossy bus loses a peer write, and the resync converges it (CREATE and DELETE for datasources, plus a no-churn case). Each has a CONTROL with no transport.
  - `cron-job-adapter.leader.test.ts`: a rejected acquire across 10 ticks gives one warning and no rejection, recovery logs once, a release rejection is absorbed, and a timer-driven fire raises no unhandled rejection.
- Forced test edits: none. The authz bridge harness now hands back a stable `objectql` service carrying a `writeEpoch` seam; no existing assertion changed.
- Test resolution (from `pnpm check:test-source-alias`):
  - `service-cluster-redis/vitest.config.ts` aliases `@objectstack/core` and `@objectstack/service-job` to source. It previously re-exported the shared preset, and it keeps the preset's one setting.
  - The datasource convergence test loads `@objectstack/driver-sql` at module top.
  - `service-datasource/vitest.config.ts` aliases `@objectstack/driver-memory` to source. A module-top import of it would have been a new arrival in `pnpm check:driver-memory-census` (#6664). The alias retires that package's shrink-only `@objectstack/driver-memory` entry in `scripts/check-test-source-alias.mjs`, as that gate requires. That is a one-token edit outside the card's file surface.
- Ablations (each through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`; every one landed and went red, and every restore left `git diff HEAD` empty):

  | Ablation | Red tests |
  | --- | --- |
  | A1: acquire try/catch removed | 3 red, including the timer-driven unhandled-rejection pin |
  | A2: cron warn latch | 3 red, 10 warnings instead of 1 |
  | A3: liveness warn latch | 2 red, 26 instead of 1 |
  | A4: resync before every source is back | 1 red |
  | A5: redaction | 2 red |
  | A6: `commandTimeout` removed | the black-hole case times out at 10 s |
  | A7: resync on first connect | 3 red |
  | B1: metadata bridge shutdown detach | 1 red |
  | B2: authz shutdown detach | 1 red |
  | B3 / B4 / B5: metadata, datasource and automation no-transport guards | 1 red each |
  | B6: datasource connectivity check (no churn) | 1 red |

  B5 first stayed green against a weaker control. That control was strengthened in its own commit, and B5 then went red.

## Acceptance notes

- The `metadata.mutated` registry lane (lane 2) has no resync seam yet. It still converges per item on delivered signals and fully at boot. I recommend a follow-up card.
- Against a black-holed store the health reads `unknown` or `up` until the socket errors. The command bound, not the health, is what stops a caller hanging.
- A `SET NX` that timed out client-side may still land on the server, so a lock can stay held until its TTL. The fire is skipped, never run twice.
- Out of the file surface:
  - The shared cache's derived connection (`service-cache/src/cache-service-plugin.ts`, `base.duplicate()`) has no `error` listener of its own, so it still prints ioredis' `Unhandled error event` during an outage.
  - The messaging dispatchers warn on each backed-off tick.
  - `check:test-source-alias`'s source-reach remedy for a lazily loaded `@objectstack/driver-memory` (a module-top import) is a binding that `check:driver-memory-census` refuses. Any edited test that reaches the default driver factory meets that conflict. This PR resolves it by aliasing to source.

  These are left for a follow-up.
- The `!` in the title: on a single node nothing changes. On the redis driver the only new default is the 2 s command bound. The changeset is `patch` with no BREAKING banner. The seat re-states whether the `!` stands.

## Verification

- Per touched package, a full `vitest run`, `pnpm typecheck` and package-scoped lint (root eslint on the directory, `--no-inline-config`) all exit 0:

  | Package | Test files | Tests |
  | --- | --- | --- |
  | service-cluster | 9 | 130 |
  | service-cluster-redis | 4 | 41 (the real-redis file included) |
  | service-job | 11 | 125 |
  | metadata | 71 | 984 |
  | service-datasource | 74 | 1299 |
  | service-automation | 266 | 3458 |

  The datasource suite was re-run on the final head. Lint on `scripts/check-test-source-alias.mjs` exits 0.
- Full dogfood (`pnpm --filter @objectstack/dogfood test`, on `2cb8ab79`): 440 test files passed and 3 skipped; 3652 tests passed and 41 skipped. The only commit after it touches test resolution and a gate registry, not package source.
- `dispatch-gates.mjs --commands` was derived on the final head `bf098837` and gave 105 commands. Each was run (all exit 0) and reconciled with `--ran`: 105 derived, 105 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED.
